posts.text:
I have to be honest with America today. This thing about Marco Rubio — it has been keeping me up at night. And I do not think even Trump has fully noticed it yet. Look at every single photo from China. Every meeting. Every ceremony. Every moment. Trump is there. And right beside him — always — is Marco Rubio. Not in front. Not behind. Right beside. Like a shield. Like a brother. Like a man who made one quiet decision before boarding that plane — wherever my President goes — I go too. And then I thought about what Marco left behind to be in those photos. His children are growing up right now. At the age when a child needs his father the most. And Marco is in Beijing. In meetings. In ceremonies. Away from home. Again. And he never mentions it. Never complains. Never once says — look what I am giving up for this country. He just shows up.
Every single time. And I thought about what Trump said when he asked that crowd — should JD get 2028. And the room erupted. And Trump smiled. And I thought — one day someone will ask the same question about Marco Rubio. And the answer will already be written in every photo from China.
In every room he entered beside his President. In every moment he chose America over his family. Without asking anyone to notice. Tonight say one prayer for Marco Rubio. For the son of a bartender who is standing in every room that matters. God bless you Marco. America sees you. 🙏🇺🇲 Do you see Marco Rubio as America’s future — tell me honestly below.

posts.text:
The "rich are fleeing high-tax states" story doesn't hold up, per Fortune.

The states with the most progressive tax systems, including California and New York, have the highest concentration of millionaires in the country, per a Fiscal Policy Institute analysis of IRS data.

And their millionaire populations have grown since 2010.

When California raised its top tax rate to 13.3% in 2012, critics warned the rich would leave.

About 138 did. That's 0.04% of the 312,000 people hit by the tax, per a Stanford-led study.

"Taxes aren't really high enough for them to be sensitive."
